```python
import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

# Job data
jobs = {
    "0": {"processing_time": 65, "due_date": 84, "weight": 10},
    "1": {"processing_time": 74, "due_date": 91, "weight": 3},
    "2": {"processing_time": 74, "due_date": 541, "weight": 1},
    "3": {"processing_time": 33, "due_date": 305, "weight": 6},
    "4": {"processing_time": 56, "due_date": 259, "weight": 7},
    "5": {"processing_time": 80, "due_date": 347, "weight": 3},
    "6": {"processing_time": 53, "due_date": 286, "weight": 5},
    "7": {"processing_time": 75, "due_date": 238, "weight": 3},
    "8": {"processing_time": 76, "due_date": 546, "weight": 9},
    "9": {"processing_time": 5, "due_date": 370, "weight": 5},
    "10": {"processing_time": 41, "due_date": 325, "weight": 7},
    "11": {"processing_time": 78, "due_date": 89, "weight": 7},
    "12": {"processing_time": 11, "due_date": 548, "weight": 3},
    "13": {"processing_time": 15, "due_date": 299, "weight": 1},
    "14": {"processing_time": 49, "due_date": 478, "weight": 7}
}

# Create a new model
model = gp.Model("single_machine_scheduling")
model.Params.OutputFlag = 0

# Create variables
n = len(jobs)
x = model.addVars(n, n, vtype=GRB.BINARY, name="x")
C = model.addVars(n, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="C")
T = model.addVars(n, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="T")

# Set objective
model.setObjective(gp.quicksum(jobs[str(j)]["weight"] * T[j] for j in range(n)), GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Add constraints
model.addConstrs((gp.quicksum(x[i, j] for j in range(n)) == 1 for i in range(n)), name="assign_once")
model.addConstrs((gp.quicksum(x[j, i] for j in range(n)) == 1 for i in range(n)), name="assigned_once")

model.addConstrs((C[j] >= jobs[str(i)]["processing_time"] + gp.quicksum(
    jobs[str(k)]["processing_time"] * x[k, j] for k in range(n) if k != i) for i in range(n) for j in range(n)), name="completion_time")

model.addConstrs((T[j] >= C[j] - jobs[str(j)]["due_date"] for j in range(n)), name="tardiness")

# Optimize model
model.optimize()

# Extract the sequence
sequence = [j for j in range(n) for i in range(n) if x[i, j].X > 0.5]

# Calculate the objective value
objective_value = model.ObjVal

# Output the result
import json
result = {"sequence": sequence, "objective_value": objective_value}
print(json.dumps(result))
```
